D009-D001_h019.question:
It’s been a rough few months. About four months now I’ve just felt…hollow, really. It’s not even sadness most days, more like I’m just not there inside. Things I used to enjoy—reading the paper, doing the garden, helping with the grandkids’ homework—I just can’t be bothered to start. My wife nudges me about little chores and I just sit and stare at them. I keep going over old mistakes from work, tiny things from years ago, and I lie in bed replaying them, telling myself I was useless.

I’ve noticed I’m forgetting where I put my glasses, why I walked into a room, or the names of old colleagues. It worries me, but I also know my mind just doesn’t seem to lock onto things like it used to. The last few weeks I’ve even found myself quietly planning, in detail, how I might end it—where I’d go so my wife wouldn’t find me, what I’d use.

Oddly, about three weeks ago I also had a spell where my mood kept swinging—one moment almost upbeat, the next snapping at my wife over nothing. I couldn’t sit still; I’d be pacing around the house, starting little projects and then abandoning them. Any small sound—the kettle, a car outside, the TV—would pull my attention away from whatever I was doing. It didn’t really stop me functioning, but it felt like my mind and body were revved up and jumpy, even against that background of emptiness.
D009-D001_h019.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D009-D001_h019.answer: D & B. Bipolar II Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D009-D001_h020.question:
It’s been a strange year for me. About six months ago I slipped into this…flat place. For four months or so, I’ve felt like I’m moving through cotton. I don’t really feel much of anything anymore, even when my grandchildren visit. Things that used to make me proud, like keeping the house nice or finishing a knitting project, just feel pointless. 

I keep beating myself up over the smallest things—if I misplace a bill or forget to call someone back, I start telling myself I’m useless, that maybe my husband wouldn’t have suffered so much if I’d been a better wife. I’ve even gathered up some of my old pain pills a couple of times and thought it might be better if I just didn’t wake up, though I haven’t gone through with it.  

My memory worries me. I lose track of where I put my keys or why I walked into a room, and then I can’t focus enough to retrace my steps.  

Then, a few weeks ago—about three weeks now—I swung the other way. I’ve been touchy, snapping at the TV or the neighbor over nothing, pacing around, starting little chores and not finishing them. Every noise, a car outside or the kettle whistling, pulls my attention away. I’m busier, but not really getting more done.
D009-D001_h020.options:
A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
D009-D001_h020.answer: D & B. Bipolar II Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D009-D001_h021.question:
I guess what’s been bothering me started a little over a year ago. I used to love teaching classes, planning sequences, all of that, but lately I just can’t get myself to start things. Even answering emails or planning a simple flow feels like this huge mountain. People ask me a normal question and I catch myself pausing way too long, like my brain is moving through mud before I can get the words out.

I’m tired all the time, even on days when I sleep a full night and don’t do many classes. It’s this heavy, drained feeling in my body. I cry more than I’d like to admit—sometimes after class, or even on my mat at home, over stuff that doesn’t seem that big. It’s been like this most of the past year, and it’s definitely made it hard to keep up with my schedule and income.

But then there was this stretch, maybe three months, when I felt almost the opposite. I was unusually upbeat, full of energy, signing up to sub extra classes, starting new online projects at the same time. I could go several nights sleeping very little and still feel wired and “on,” so I just kept going. It didn’t really mess up my life, but it felt…not quite like my usual self.
D009-D001_h021.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D009-D001_h021.answer: B & D. Bipolar II Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D009-D001_h022.question:
It’s hard to put into words, but over the last year or so I just haven’t felt like myself. For more than a year now, everything has felt heavy and slow. I move like I’m walking through water. Even getting dressed or making tea feels like it takes all my strength. I used to be proud of keeping the house nice and staying on top of things; now, even when I manage to do something, I just feel… nothing. No sense of “good job,” just this flatness. I feel drained most of the time, and people say I seem distant, like I’m not really reacting to anything.

Then there was this stretch, maybe three months, where I swung the other way. I was on edge and snappy over little things—a cup in the wrong place, the TV too loud. I couldn’t sit still; I was constantly pacing, tidying, starting little projects around the house. I went several nights barely sleeping at all, but it didn’t bother me then—I just kept going, cleaning cupboards at 3 a.m. and reorganizing old photo albums. I didn’t think it was a “problem” at the time, but looking back, it felt like I was driven by a motor I couldn’t shut off.
D009-D001_h022.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D009-D001_h022.answer: B & D. Bipolar II Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D009-D001_h023.question:
I guess the main thing is my mood and energy swing around, but not in a way I can easily pin down. For the last year or so, I’ve mostly felt kind of hollow, like I’m just going through the motions. Stuff I used to like doing with the kids, crafts, baking, even watching shows, doesn’t really feel like anything anymore. I move really slowly, like my body’s heavy. Even walking up the stairs or unloading the dishwasher feels like a lot, and I get tired so fast. My husband says I shuffle around the house. It’s gotten bad enough that I’ve let laundry and school emails pile up, which is not like me.

But then there was this stretch a few months back, maybe around three months, where I was the opposite. I was on edge all the time, snapping at the kids over little things, really short-tempered. At the same time I had this restless energy, couldn’t sit still, always needing to clean something or start some new project. I was sleeping fewer hours but waking up like I didn’t really need more. It didn’t ruin anything in my life, but it felt odd compared to how drained I’ve mostly been feeling.
D009-D001_h023.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D009-D001_h023.answer: B & D. Bipolar II Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D009-D001_h024.question:
I guess the main thing is I just don’t feel like myself anymore, and it’s been going on for a while. For a little over a year I’ve felt really low most days—kind of heavy and flat. I drag myself to my data entry job, but my speed’s dropped a lot and I make more mistakes. Even simple stuff like checking an email or filling a spreadsheet makes my brain feel tired really fast, like I’ve run a marathon just from thinking.

I’ve pulled back from people. I avoid group chats at work and usually say no when coworkers or even my sisters ask to meet up. At home, my husband notices I just sit there, picking at the skin around my nails or getting up and pacing for no real reason. I feel restless but also exhausted. It’s like I can’t relax in my own body.

Before this long “down” stretch, there was about three months where I felt almost the opposite—like I had way too much energy. I’d be up late, sometimes almost all night, just moving around, cleaning, organizing files, starting new projects online, and I didn’t really feel like I needed sleep. My mood would swing a lot then: I’d feel on top of things and strangely upbeat, then suddenly snappy or annoyed over little comments from my husband or coworkers. I liked how productive I felt, but it also made it harder to sit still at my desk or focus on one task at a time.
D009-D001_h024.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D009-D001_h024.answer: B & D. Bipolar II Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D009-D001_h025.question:
I guess the main thing is I just don’t feel like myself anymore. For a little over a year, most days I’m just flat and dragged out. Stuff I used to like—tinkering with old car batteries, watching games with my buddies—just feels like a chore. I’m exhausted all the time, even if I sleep a full night, and I’ve been moving around the house like I’m wading through mud. At the same time, I can’t sit still; my leg’s always bouncing, I’m pacing around the kitchen, picking at the skin on my fingers without noticing. My wife says I look “checked out” and it’s been affecting work; I’m slower on jobs and I put things off.

But then there are these stretches—like the last three months—where I swing the other way. My mood flips fast: one minute I’m joking around, feeling on top of everything, the next I’m snapping over small stuff. I’ll suddenly take on way more solar jobs than usual, start projects all over the house at once, and barely feel like I need sleep. I’ll stay up late rewiring something or planning new installs, and I don’t really feel tired, just kind of wired, until it all dips again and I’m back to feeling low and worn out.
D009-D001_h025.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D009-D001_h025.answer: B & D. Bipolar II Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
